root_cause: The CachingTest.LoadMultiWithConfig_race is a known intermittently-failing Windows test that exercises multi-threaded model loading with a mock plugin. It uses GMock EXPECT_CALL to assert the exact number of import_model calls across threads, but under Windows CI runner scheduling, the thread interleaving varies enough to sometimes produce a different call count than expected. This is unrelated to the PR changes (ONNX FE GroupQueryAttention). It has been observed 8 times previously across unrelated PRs. The NPU TF test step failure appears to be a secondary pre-existing issue with aten ops not in the decomp table (warnings only) or a model-hub connectivity issue.
reproduction_steps: N/A - race condition is non-deterministic and Windows-runner-specific. To reproduce: run the ov_core_unit_tests binary with filter CachingTest multiple times on a Windows machine.
recommended_actions: Re-trigger the failed CI run - the race condition is transient and the test should pass on retry.
Track the LoadMultiWithConfig_race flakiness via the existing issue tracker and consider adding GTEST_SKIP() or reducing thread concurrency in the mock test.
prevention_strategies: The LoadMultiWithConfig_race test is a known flaky test on Windows. Consider marking it with GTEST_ALLOW_UNINSTANTIATED_PARAMETERIZED_TEST or reducing expected call counts to ranges. This failure has occurred 8+ times across unrelated PRs and is not caused by the PR under test.
